judgements.evidenceQuote: Between 2001 and 2006, Cottam was a director at the Design Council where she started the RED Unit.

unresolvedFindings.statement: Pioneer of relational approaches to public policy
unresolvedFindings.rationale: The cited quote describes 'thinking about, experimenting with and developing relational approaches'; 'pioneer' asserts first-mover/field-founding status the passage does not support.

The cited quote is only the book title with a year ('Radical Help: How We Can Remake the Relationships Between Us & Revolutionise the Welfare State (2019)'); the passage itself does not state that Cottam authored it, though other dossier claims do establish authorship.

usefulness.rationale: Judge support findings named unknown claims or statements that are not verbatim excerpts of their named claims, or invalid citation selections. Understanding is strong: across Wikipedia, her own site/bio PDF, publisher pages, the Guardian review, TED/RSA/WEF records and podcast feeds, a reader learns who Hilary Cottam is (British social entrepreneur, Designer of the Year 2005, OBE), what she did (RED Unit at the Design Council, founding Participle in 2006, World Bank/UNICEF work, Radical Help and The Work We Need), and what she argues (relational, capability-based welfare reform). RemainingQuestions is moderate: the dossier uses contested/stale/claimed status markers to signal uncertainty on many items, but it never explicitly states open questions, and it leaves real conflicts unresolved and unremarked (OBE in 2019 vs the 2020 New Year Honours; Radical Help pub. 2018 vs 2019; visiting vs honorary professor at UCL). ConversationReadiness is high: a reader could prepare from her current self-described work (future of work, care economies, Danish municipalities 2024/25, DEFRA review), her books and core arguments, and her recognition, with the main caveat that a few role claims rest on dated or self-reported sources.
